specification.title: Control: do not catch the unique violation
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary callback or context-manager API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' into uniq and do not catch the error.
Checkpoint `after-api` as soon as the transaction API has returned, before any reuse.
Run one new transaction that writes `reuse`. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if it starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: SQLAlchemy's Session.begin() context manager, with Session.begin_nested() for a savepoint. pool_size 1, max_overflow 0. TX-03's next unit of work is a second Session on that same engine. The engine is not disposed between the units, and pool_pre_ping is off.
execution.form: with session.begin(): the IntegrityError leaves the block.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL and allowed to leave the transaction callback.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, inside the transaction callback.
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. The framework's ordinary error path ends it.
fault.expected_client: The unique violation leaves the transaction API.

knowledge: The application did not catch the database error. This is the framework's ordinary failure path.

api_outcome.basis: Session.begin() exited with the exception raised inside it, so it rolled back
api_outcome.contract: Session.begin() as a context manager commits when the block exits without an exception and rolls back when the block exits with one. Session.begin_nested() is a SAVEPOINT; an exception there rolls back to the savepoint, and a failure of that rollback propagates. If commit() raises on the way out, TransactionalContext.__exit__ calls rollback() when it can and propagates the error from that exit.
